Initial laboratory abnormalities included leucocytosis (26.3 G/L), thrombocytosis (720 G/L), anemia (Hb 11.1 g/dl), impaired coagulation parameters (INR 1.19, normal 0.85–1.15; antithrombin III 28%, normal 80–130%), hypomagnesemia (0.53 mmol/L, normal 0.7–0.95 mmol/L), elevated transaminases (ASAT 67 U/L; ALAT 65 U/L, normal 10–50 U/L, respectively), low haptoglobin (10 mg/dL, normal 30–200

tein C was severely reduced and substituted as well as fresh frozen plasma. He received erythrocyte and thrombocyte transfusions due to persistent anemia and thrombocytopenia. Brain MRI at the age of 2.5 months showed cerebellar atrophy (Fig. 1d, e), characteristic for PMM2-CDG. At the age of 3 months he developed generalised tonic-clonic seizures that were treated with phenobarbital. The EEG showed a focal epileptic activity over the left parietal hemisphere. A: Real patient adapto-ERG recordings from both twin sisters with explicitly stated PMM2-CDG at age 4; the caption documents decreased ERG amplitudes, indicating abnormal retinal rod/cone electrophysiology consistent with the configured disease. ERG amplitude reduction is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Real patient adapto-ERG and ISCEV-standard ERG recordings from both PMM2-CDG twins at age 18; the caption states completely extinguished bilateral responses, a severe retinal electrophysiology manifestation of the configured disease. The ERG pattern itself is absent from the vocabulary and is therefore proposed. C: Real patient ERG recordings at age 41 in the same PMM2-CDG twin sisters; the caption and in-text text state unchanged, completely extinguished ERG traces for both eyes. This supports a persistent retinal electrophysiology manifestation of PMM2-CDG; the specific ERG vocabulary is missing,...

panels.figure_caption: Electroretinographic findings in twin sisters (patient 1 and patient 2) with PMM2-CDG at the age of 4 years (A), 18 years (B) and 41 years (C). A: 1980: Adapto ERG revealed decreased amplitudes, more obvious for patient 2. B: 1995: On adapto ERG, repsonses were entirely extinguished bilaterally. This exam was now completed with an ERG using the ISCEV standard; no recordable dark adapted or light adapted response was observed. C: 2018: ERG revealed unchanged findings.
in_text_mentions: A white flash is shown immediately followed by a dim orange flash (using a Wratten orange number 26 filter) and the ERG responses to these stimuli are measured (respectively white and 0’ in Figure 1A (Fig. 1)). A normal cone response consists of an a-wave and a b1-wave. These responses are followed by a period of 15’ of dark adaptation to enlarge rod contribution of the ERG response to the orange flash (15’ in Figure 1A (Fig. 1)). In normal subjects, a later b2 rod wave will follow the initial a-wave and b1-wave. For patient 1 (Figure 1A (Fig. 1)), these 3 waves could be clearly seen, but thei

moderately narrowing of the blood vessels could be seen in addition to bony spicule pigmentary deposits in the mid peripheral retina. The latter was more obvious in the first patient. In the other patient a wrinkling of the macular retinal surface was noticed (Figure 2A,B (Fig. 2)). Adapto ERG was achieved in equal conditions as 14 years earlier. At the age of 18 years, responses were completely extinguished bilaterally. This adapto ERG exam was now completed with an ERG using the ISCEV standard (Figure 1B (Fig. 1)). No recordable dark adapted or light adapted response was observed [14], [17].

. Findings of fundoscopy remained unchanged: pink optic discs, moderately narrowed blood vessels and bony spicule pigmentary deposits in the mid periphery (Figure 2C,D (Fig. 2)). The ERG examination showed completely extinguished traces for both eyes, as at the age of 18 (Figure 1C (Fig. 1)). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed severe attenuation of the outer retina starting from the perimacular area; in the central macular area, the normal outer retinal structure was preserved. Drusenoïd-like changes could also be observed, more obvious in the second patient (Figure 3A,B (Fig. 3)) [17].

source_variant.figure_caption: Electroretinographic findings in twin sisters (patient 1 and patient 2) with PMM2-CDG at the age of 4 years (A), 18 years (B) and 41 years (C). A: 1980: Adapto ERG revealed decreased amplitudes, more obvious for patient 2. B: 1995: On adapto ERG, repsonses were entirely extinguished bilaterally. This exam was now completed with an ERG using the ISCEV standard; no recordable dark adapted or light adapted response was observed. C: 2018: ERG revealed unchanged findings.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'severe attenuation of the outer retina starting from the perimacular area is shown. In the central macular area, the normal outer retinal structure was preserved' (retinal degeneration/rod-cone dystrophy correlate); in-text: bony spicule pigmentary deposits and completely extinguished ERG traces.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient OCT B-scans (OD and OS) of patient 1, a 41-year-old with PMM2-CDG (article title and caption explicitly state twin sisters with PMM2-CDG). The images show perimacular outer retinal attenuation with preserved central macular outer retina, the structural correlate of the retinal degeneration/rod-cone dystrophy (retinitis pigmentosa spectrum) that is a recognized PMM2-CDG manifestation; white arrows annotate the attenuated segments. Disease attribution is direct and findings are clearly visible, so the panel qualifies. B: Real patient OCT B-scans (OD and OS) of patient 2, the second of the twin sisters with PMM2-CDG at age 41 (caption and article title). Same perimacular outer retinal attenuation as panel A, with more obvious drusenoid-like changes, consistent with the retinal degeneration (retinitis pigmentosa spectrum) of PMM2-CDG. panels.figure_caption: OCT examination in twin sisters with PPM2-CDG at the age of 41 For patient 1 (A) and patient 2 (B), severe attenuation of the outer retina starting from the perimacular area is shown. In the central macular area, the normal outer retinal structure was preserved. Drusenoïd like changes can also be observed, more obvious in the second patient.
in_text_mentions: . Findings of fundoscopy remained unchanged: pink optic discs, moderately narrowed blood vessels and bony spicule pigmentary deposits in the mid periphery (Figure 2C,D (Fig. 2)). The ERG examination showed completely extinguished traces for both eyes, as at the age of 18 (Figure 1C (Fig. 1)). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed severe attenuation of the outer retina starting from the perimacular area; in the central macular area, the normal outer retinal structure was preserved. Drusenoïd-like changes could also be observed, more obvious in the second patient (Figure 3A,B (Fig. 3)) [17].
